source.title: Deep Gradient Boosting -- Layer-wise Input Normalization of Neural Networks

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Compares a normalized-gradient optimizer (NDGB) with SGD on held-out benchmark performance, testing whether a gradient-normalization approach has worse generalization. It does not test the standard adaptive optimizers named in V4.
record.gate_note: The paper reports held-out performance for NDGB and SGD. Its DGB results are not rows for V4 because DGB is not the adaptive optimizer behavior named there. MNIST training-accuracy curves are described as faster convergence, but do not quantify the train–test gap.
record.test_reason: The study uses prior findings about SGD's generalization to motivate DGB and evaluates its own DGB and NDGB methods. NDGB normalizes layer-output pseudo-residuals within a different, matrix-based update rule; these comparisons do not isolate the adaptive-optimizer behavior under limited tuning named in V4. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that DGB outperforms SGD in some tasks but underperforms on tasks they regard as requiring stricter generalization, such as image recognition. They describe NDGB as approaching SGD's MNIST test performance and present SGD as an implicitly regularized limiting case of DGB.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces deep gradient boosting and its normalized-gradient variant, rather than testing the standard adaptive optimizers and tuning protocol described in V4.
record.method_sensitivity: Performance varies by dataset and architecture; the paper reports different test outcomes across Higgs, Reuters, HR, Air, and MNIST. For MNIST, increasing DGB's α diminishes overfitting; increasing the NDGB moment value decreased performance.

fits_no_version.finding: NDGB improves reported test performance over selected SGD configurations on Higgs and Air, gives marginal differences on Reuters, uncertain differences on HR, and similar performance on MNIST.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The held-out performance of the proposed normalized deep gradient boosting method relative to SGD depends on the dataset and training configuration.

record.problems: The paper does not test Adam or other standard adaptive optimizers, the limited-tuning protocol, or training-performance parity described in V4. It says HR error bars are too large to claim an optimizer advantage. The results concern a new method and do not establish the generalization behavior of the named adaptive methods.
record.rows_left_out: DGB rows from Tables 2–6 were not included because DGB is not the normalized-gradient variant relevant to V4; MNIST training-accuracy curves were not included because they do not quantify the train–test gap.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label generalization, and their coexistence under the same training recipe.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under the specified tuning regimes, training-performance comparisons, and the stated recovery mechanisms.
Batch-size penalties under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove them.
Dropout effects and interactions with dataset size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization gaps, and comparisons with other generalization measures.
Removing memorized examples versus removing random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Reported uncertainties are standard deviations over ten random seeds. Experiments varied architecture, batch size, learning rate, schedules, epochs, and alpha where applicable, and ran until test-set convergence; this is not the limited-tuning comparison specified in V4. Omitted DGB results and MNIST curves were already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width beyond the interpolation threshold and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.

Standard adaptive optimizers such as Adam; image-classification and language benchmarks in the stated version; limited-tuning protocol; whether training performance is equal or better; broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching to SGD, and word-level language models.
Large-batch effects and adaptations to batch size.
Dropout and its interaction with dataset size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to generalization gaps.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: NDGB on the reported benchmark settings
reader_labels.reason: NDGB exceeds the SGD test-performance baseline on Higgs, Reuters, and Air; on MNIST the authors describe its performance as very similar to SGD (R1–R8). The study does not test the standard adaptive optimizers or tuning protocol in V4.
